author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: An early science-fiction short story from Dick's first professional period in the early 1950s, turning on a small, unsettling premise in the mode of his apprentice magazine work.
page_summary:
The Little Movement is one of Dick's early short stories, belonging to the burst of magazine fiction he produced at the very start of his professional career in the early 1950s. It survives here as a short archived text of a few pages.

Like much of his apprentice work, it takes a compact, disquieting premise and pushes it a single sharp step past the ordinary. The stories of this period are where Dick first practiced the moves that define the later fiction: an everyday surface, a small wrongness introduced, and the reader left uncertain about what is really happening.

Without overstating the ambitions of a brief early piece, this story matters as part of the foundation. It is one of the many short works from Dick's opening years that collectively taught him the craft he would carry into the novels.
